Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0056", "row_sha256": "2cddb4d42f4e27856ab95abbf52f86cc5df761244b4ab5e077553ab2708a51a4", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "okay i need a clear prompt for an inventory handoff note for Cedar Lane Food Cooperative, using the Thursday stocktake from October 16. It was done from 7:15 until 9:05 in the morning, before the Friday opening shift, and the note is for the members and staff opening on Friday. Please make the handoff useful as a record of what was counted, not a claim that anything has been reordered or fixed. Amina Patel led the count, Joel Kim checked the freezer, and Rosa Ellis checked labels and wrote down the cooler count. Say that these are physical counts at the time of the stocktake. The stocktake was in the receiving room, dry storage, cooler and freezer, and don't make it sound like there was a customer-area count too.

For dry storage, the count was 18 two-kilogram bags of oats: 16 sealed bags and two opened bags, one of those opened bags about half full. The ledger has 20 bags, so there's a difference of two, but don't guess why. Black beans were 24 cans, chickpeas were 13 cans and lentils were 8 cans. The ledger has 12 cans of chickpeas, so the physical count is one higher. Tomato sauce was five sealed jars on the shelf. Rosa said, “The label says six, but I counted five sealed jars.” Keep the quote as spoken and make clear it is about the jars, not another item. The shelf label says six jars, and that is the source of the mismatch; no need to decide whether a jar was taken or misplaced.

There was also a rice delivery, one unopened 10-kilogram bag, brought in on Wednesday at 6:40 p.m. The bag was in dry storage at count time and was included in the physical count, but it had not yet been entered in the ledger. Keep that distinct from the oat, chickpea and sauce differences. Don't say the delivery was late, approved, or missing paperwork; all we know is the delivery time and that the ledger entry had not been made. There are four cartons of vegetable stock beside it, each carton containing six one-litre packs. That is a carton count and a pack size, not 24 separate cartons.

In the produce area, there were 11 crates of apples. Four bruised apples were set aside in a shallow tray beside the crates, and the crate count should stay 11; don't subtract the loose apples from it or imply that the whole crate was bruised. There were three crates of potatoes and two bags of spinach marked for the cooler. The note should keep the apples, potatoes and spinach as separate lines. No weight was recorded for those crates or bags, so don't convert them into pounds or kilograms. A hand-written card on the potato crate says “use these first,” but nobody said when they were delivered. Include the card wording if useful, without turning it into a dated instruction.

For the cooler, Rosa counted nine cartons of oat milk, seven cartons of whole milk and five blocks of tofu. Two oat milk cartons have a best-before date of October 18, and the remaining seven have October 24. Four whole milk cartons have October 17 dates; the other three have October 20. Two tofu blocks are dated October 19 and three are dated October 21. These are dates as written on the packages; don't call anything expired on October 16 or decide that it must be discarded. The cooler display read 4 degrees Celsius at 8:35 a.m. during the count. There is no second temperature reading, and no temperature target was recorded, so report that one reading without claiming a trend or compliance.

Joel counted 14 loaves of bread and six bags of spinach in the freezer. At 8:10 he found the freezer door not fully shut. He closed it, and at 8:35 the display read minus 12 degrees Celsius. Keep the timing and sequence clear, but don't state how long the door was open or what caused it. Do not infer food safety or say any stock was damaged. The spinach in the freezer is separate from the two bags marked for the cooler. There's no freezer reading from before 8:35, so avoid presenting the number as the temperature for the whole morning.

Could you make the note easy to scan for someone starting a shift, with a short opening that gives the date, time and people involved, then sections for dry storage, produce, cooler and freezer? Within each section, list the counted items and include any ledger difference, label information, dates or temperature that belongs there. A small numbered section is okay for follow-up items, but only include things the count actually identifies: the oat and chickpea ledger differences, the sauce label/count mismatch, the rice ledger entry not yet made, and the freezer door observation. Don't assign anyone a job or suggest a fix. Keep counts and units exact, and distinguish sealed, opened, loose, dated, and packaged items where those details matter. If an item has an unknown weight or an unknown cause, leave it unknown rather than filling in a likely answer.

One privacy detail matters for the handoff. do not publish photos of the stockroom, shelves, cooler, freezer, or inventory sheets. Typed counts may be shared in the members-only weekly bulletin. That allowed action is about typed counts only; it doesn't change the photo restriction. The note itself can use the facts above, and it should not imply that photos are needed to verify any count. Please keep the language direct and practical rather than making a narrative out of the morning.

There was no count of the customer area, no reorder decision, and no report from a later shift. Keep the last paragraph focused on a separate closing detail: the receiving room's paper sign-in sheet shows the stocktake ended at 9:05 a.m., and it has no notes after that time. Don't treat the lack of later notes as evidence that nobody entered the room, and don't add a general summary or recommendation at the end.", "output": "Write a clear, practical inventory handoff note for Cedar Lane Food Cooperative’s Friday opening members and staff, based on the physical stocktake conducted Thursday, October 16, from 7:15 to 9:05 a.m. Amina Patel led the count, Joel Kim checked the freezer, and Rosa Ellis checked labels and recorded the cooler count. State that the figures are physical counts at the time of the stocktake. The count covered the receiving room, dry storage, cooler, and freezer; it did not cover the customer area. Present the information as a record of what was counted, not as confirmation that anything has been reordered or fixed.

Organize the note with a short opening followed by sections for dry storage, produce, cooler, and freezer. Make it easy to scan during a shift. Preserve all counts, units, dates, labels, and distinctions between sealed, opened, loose, dated, and packaged items. Do not fill in unknown weights, causes, or other missing details.

**Dry storage**
- Oats: 18 two-kilogram bags, comprising 16 sealed bags and two opened bags. One opened bag was about half full. The ledger lists 20 bags, a difference of two; do not speculate about the cause.
- Black beans: 24 cans. Chickpeas: 13 cans. The ledger lists 12 cans of chickpeas, one fewer than the physical count. Lentils: 8 cans.
- Tomato sauce: five sealed jars on the shelf. The shelf label says six. Preserve Rosa’s quote: “The label says six, but I counted five sealed jars.” Make clear that the quote concerns the sauce jars. Do not guess whether a jar was taken or misplaced.
- Rice: one unopened 10-kilogram bag, delivered Wednesday at 6:40 p.m. It was in dry storage and included in the physical count, but had not yet been entered in the ledger. Do not call the delivery late, approved, or missing paperwork.
- Vegetable stock: four cartons beside the rice, each containing six one-litre packs. Distinguish four cartons from 24 separate cartons.

**Produce**
There were 11 crates of apples. Four bruised apples were set aside in a shallow tray beside the crates; retain the crate count of 11 and do not suggest a whole crate was bruised. There were three crates of potatoes and two bags of spinach marked for the cooler. Keep apples, potatoes, and spinach as separate lines, and do not convert the crates or bags to a weight. The potato crate had a handwritten card reading “use these first.” Include that wording if useful, but do not assign it a delivery date.

**Cooler**
Rosa counted nine cartons of oat milk, seven cartons of whole milk, and five blocks of tofu. Two oat milk cartons are dated October 18 and the other seven October 24. Four whole milk cartons are dated October 17 and the other three October 20. Two tofu blocks are dated October 19 and three October 21. Report these as package dates; do not call anything expired on October 16 or decide that it must be discarded. The cooler display read 4 degrees Celsius at 8:35 a.m. This is the only cooler reading recorded. Do not claim a trend or compliance with a temperature target.

**Freezer**
Joel counted 14 loaves of bread and six bags of spinach. The freezer spinach is separate from the two bags marked for the cooler. At 8:10 a.m. Joel found the freezer door not fully shut and closed it. At 8:35 a.m. the display read minus 12 degrees Celsius. Keep the sequence clear, but do not state how long the door had been open, what caused it, or whether any food was unsafe or damaged. No earlier freezer reading was recorded, so do not present the 8:35 reading as the temperature for the whole morning.

A small numbered follow-up section may list only the identified items: the oat and chickpea ledger differences, the sauce label/count mismatch, the rice entry not yet made in the ledger, and the freezer-door observation. Do not assign anyone a task or propose a fix. Keep the language direct and practical rather than turning the handoff into a narrative.

Privacy requirement: do not publish photos of the stockroom, shelves, cooler, freezer, or inventory sheets. Typed counts may be shared in the members-only weekly bulletin. The permission applies to typed counts only and does not change the photo restriction; do not imply that photos are needed to verify a count.

There was no customer-area count, reorder decision, or report from a later shift. End with the distinct closing detail that the receiving room’s paper sign-in sheet shows the stocktake ended at 9:05 a.m. and contains no notes after that time. Do not treat the absence of later notes as proof that nobody entered the room. Do not add a general summary or recommendation at the end."}]
